title: Audio Input Jack Removal and Installation — Vehicles With SYNC
introduction:
The LINE IN and USB panel inside the floor console is your landmark. I think of its bezel as a picture frame: free the frame from the console first, then release the jack from the frame. Keeping those separate attachments straight makes this little job much less of a plastic puzzle.

This procedure covers physical removal and refitting on vehicles with SYNC. The final playback check confirms ordinary use after assembly; it is not an electrical diagnosis.

items.name: Park before working
items.detail: Park the car, apply the parking brake and keep the engine off. For the final playback check, use P with an automatic transmission or neutral with a manual, keeping the parking brake applied. Have a compatible portable music player and an audio extension cable that connects its headphone output to the round LINE IN jack. This check is for the analog input, not a USB-only media hub.

items.name: Review the applicable safety precautions
items.detail: Before starting, review the applicable warnings in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189). The relevant startup and handling precautions are included below.

items.name: Trim-removal tool
items.detail: Have a trim-removal tool of the type pictured ready for removing the audio input jack bezel.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: If equipped, disable remote start through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before beginning service around the vehicle. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, resulting in personal injury or death.

items.name: Remove the key
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from accidentally starting the engine during service. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear eye and ear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect against sharp edges
items.detail: Wear protective gloves when handling components or parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: Raise the floor console lid to open the storage compartment.
edits.why: The audio input jack bezel is inside this compartment; opening the lid exposes the working area beside the cupholders.

edits.text: Use the trim-removal tool shown to ease the audio input jack bezel out of its opening in the console storage compartment.
edits.why: The bezel is the surrounding panel carrying the LINE IN and USB openings. Removing it exposes the rear electrical connections before the jack itself is released.

edits.text: At the rear of the bezel, press the locking tab on each electrical connector toward its connector body, then unplug the connectors from the audio input jack.
edits.why: The rear-view inset shows the connector locks being depressed. Releasing these locks frees the wiring connections so the bezel and jack can be handled separately from the harness.

edits.text: Viewed from behind the bezel, move the upper retaining tab upward and the lower retaining tab downward, away from the audio input jack, to release it.
edits.why: These opposing tabs hold the jack in the bezel mounting frame. They are separate from the locking tabs on the electrical connectors.

edits.text: With the retaining tabs released, withdraw the audio input jack away from the bezel mounting frame toward the exposed electrical-connector side, as viewed from behind the bezel.
edits.why: The rear-view drawing shows the jack leaving toward its electrical-connector side. Keeping that viewpoint clear avoids trying to push it through the visible face of the bezel.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: insert the audio input jack from the rear electrical-connector side toward the bezel mounting frame until the upper and lower retaining tabs engage. Reconnect the electrical connectors, seat the bezel back in the console opening, and close the floor console lid.
edits.why:
The jack must be retained in the bezel before the wiring is reconnected and the bezel is returned to the console. Engaged jack tabs and connector locks restore the attachments released during removal.

After the assembly is completely refitted, perform this ordinary playback check while stationary. Switch the engine, radio and portable player off; keep the parking brake applied and select P with an automatic or neutral with a manual. Connect the player’s headphone output to the round LINE IN jack using the compatible audio cable. Turn the radio on, select a tuned FM station or CD and set a comfortable listening volume. Switch the player on and set its volume to half its maximum. Press AUX until LINE or LINE IN appears, start playback, then adjust the player volume to match the FM or CD level by switching between the sources. You should hear the player through the vehicle speakers.

Finish with the radio and player off. Keep the engine and ignition off and remove the key before any further connector inspection. If playback is abnormal, use the matching audio diagnostic procedure rather than treating this check as proof that the new jack is faulty. The method comes from the Mustang Owner’s Manual, Audio Input Jack section. Never connect or adjust the player while the vehicle is moving; secure it and its cable before driving.
